groups.text: In Reactor, demand travels up the chain.
The subscriber calls request(n), which means I can take n more.
A source like Flux.range sends at most n, then waits.
A ticker can't wait.
Flux.interval ticks once a millisecond, whatever you request.
Behind it, a screen asks for one tick at a time, and takes ten milliseconds to draw it.
Tick one comes before anyone asked for it, and the stream fails.
The onBackpressure operators let you choose what happens instead.
Each one requests unbounded, so the source never overflows, and then decides what to do with the ticks nobody asked for.
onBackpressureBuffer with no size keeps every tick in a queue.
The screen gets zero, one, two, three, all in order.
But after twenty frames, the ticker is at two hundred four.
More than one hundred eighty ticks wait in memory, and the backlog grows until the heap runs out.
Give the buffer a size, like ten.
While the screen draws tick zero, ticks one to ten fill it.
Then a tick finds no room.
The buffer cancels the source and fails.
The error waits behind the buffered ticks.
The screen still gets zero to eleven, in order, and then the error.
onBackpressureDrop keeps nothing.
Each tick that arrives while nobody is asking is thrown away.
So the screen sees ticks about eleven apart, and in twenty frames about two hundred are dropped.
onBackpressureLatest keeps one slot, and each new tick replaces the one before.
When the screen asks, it gets the newest: about every tenth tick.
onBackpressureError fails at once, at the first tick nobody asked for.
None of these slows the source down.
They only decide what to lose.
Real backpressure needs a source that honours request(n).
So pick by the kind of feed.
Prices, positions and statuses want latest, because newer replaces older.
Samples and metrics can be dropped.
Card authorizations and audit events must not be lost, so they get a bounded buffer that fails loudly.
Error is for feeds where falling behind is a bug.
And the unbounded buffer suits almost nothing.
In Kotlin Flow, a slow collector simply suspends the emitter.
When a buffer sits between them, conflate keeps the newest, like onBackpressureLatest, and a full buffer suspends the emitter instead of failing.
